tool.name: DataServicePillagerTool

param.name: service_endpoint
param.dialogReference:
Arrrr! Enter ye service url here.

F'r a single layer, make sure ye has the layer id number. Else, it grabs all the layers!

Example:

Single layer: http://www.myserver.com/arcgis/rest/services/Service/MapServer/0

All layers: http://www.myserver.com/arcgis/rest/services/Service/MapServer

param.name: output_workspace
param.dialogReference: The location where ye want to stash the data. Yon filegeodatabase is best, can be a folder or sde, it's up ter ye. If it be a folder or filegeodatabase, twill be made fer ye.

param.name: max_tries
param.dialogReference: If yer query fails, we tries again this many times.

param.name: sleep_time
param.dialogReference: This be the number of seconds we sleeps afore tryin' agin

param.name: strict_mode
param.dialogReference: Yer service should support JSON, so True checks fer it. If ye wants to take yer chances, try False at yer own risk.

param.name: username
param.dialogReference: Sail ho! If ye knows someone on the inside, put their name here to git up to the gate safely.

param.name: password
param.dialogReference: No quarter! Enter ye secret password to get past the scurvy guards.

param.name: referring_domain
param.dialogReference:
Not needed for *.arcgis.com services, cos we knows that one.

If ye username or password is fer a different url as yer service url, enter it here.

Fer example, federated server needs a referring domain for portal cos that's where ye logs in.

param.name: existing_token
param.dialogReference: If ye have a valid token for accessing the data, enter it here. Overrides password and username, and ye don't need this if you have a password and username.

param.name: query_str
param.dialogReference:
Takes yer chances here. A wise man gave me this advice:

This needs to be a valid SQL query used to limit the data, and must be well formed and valid as there is no way to test it prior to running! It is suggested you generate a SQL query suitable for the data from the REST endpoint "Where" box and paste it in. It will be automatically parsed for the url query. An example of a valid query might be ST_ABBREV IN ('WA', 'OR')

The SQL string will be added to the where clause used to select and download the data. As the Pillager also does an OID where clause, there may be cases where the SQL you pass in causes nothing to be returned. You should always check that the SQL is correct.

param.name: ignore_ssl_verification
param.dialogReference: By default the tool does not ignore SSL validation. This may fail on old certs etc. Check the box to disable verification.

param.name: ca_bundle_path
param.dialogReference: A path to a custom CA Bundle file. If provided, will use this instead of the default OS certs.

param.name: create_empty_schema
param.displayname: Create Empty Schema If No Rows
param.dialogReference: If ye choose this path, we creates an output even if it's empty.

param.name: overwrite_output
param.dialogReference: Takin' no care to preserve what ye might already have, we creates it anyways.

param.name: include_attachments
param.dialogReference: When ye want all the goodies, but beware, can take longer and takes up a lot of space (we recommends you select the cleanup option)

param.name: clean_up_temp_attachments_data
param.dialogReference: We deletes the temporary stuff as we go, so yer storage can keeps up

tool.summary:
Yaar!

Like a pirate on the seven seas, this tool will rampantly pillage data from an ArcGIS Service. Handles multiple layers in a service, or just one.

If the service is secured, you will need to enter a username and password (or a valid token) to access it, unfortunately the pillager can't get past a locked gate.

The referring domain is the location for the security token service, and should be added when this differs from the root url of the service, and only if the service needs a username and password.

You can enter a token if you have one. Do not enter a username and password if you have a valid token!

Strict mode will check that the service supports JSON. Turn it off if you prefer to take yer chances...

The pillager will generate service info text files in yer output folder.
